title: Rigveda 5.22: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.22: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.22 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 335v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.22.1-4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 335v
translation.original_text:
1pra vi̍śvasāmann atri̱vad arcā̍ pāva̱kaśo̍ciṣe | yo a̍dhva̱reṣv īḍyo̱ hotā̍ ma̱ndrata̍mo vi̱śi ||
2ny a1̱̍gniṁ jā̱tave̍dasa̱ṁ dadhā̍tā de̱vam ṛ̱tvija̍m | pra ya̱jña e̍tv ānu̱ṣag a̱dyā de̱vavya̍castamaḥ ||
3ci̱ki̱tvinma̍nasaṁ tvā de̱vam martā̍sa ū̱taye̍ | vare̍ṇyasya̱ te 'va̍sa iyā̱nāso̍ amanmahi ||
4agne̍ ciki̱ddhy a1̱̍sya na̍ i̱daṁ vaca̍ḥ sahasya | taṁ tvā̍ suśipra dampate̱ stomai̍r vardha̱nty atra̍yo gī̱rbhiḥ śu̍mbha̱nty atra̍yaḥ ||
translation.text:
1LIKE Atri, Viṣvasâman! sing to him of purifying light, Who must be praised in holy rites, the Priest most welcome in the house.
2Set Jâtavedas in his place, Agni the God and Minister. Let sacrifice proceed to-day duly, comprising all the Gods.
3All mortals come to thee for aid, the God of most observant mind. Of thine excelling favour we bethink us as we long for it.
4Mark with attention this our speech, O Agni, thou victorious One. Thee, Strong-jawed! as the homestead's Lord, the Atris with their lauds exalt, the Atris beautify with songs.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 335v (numbered 8v by the scribe) (OPenn image 336, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.22.1 ‹pra viśva-sāman atri-vat arca›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 336r (numbered 9r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.23.2 ‹pṛtanāsaham rayim sahasvaḥ ā›. Verses 5.22.1-4 end on this page.

2ni | agnim | jāta-vedasam | dadhāta | devam | ṛtvijam | pra | yajñaḥ | etu | ānuṣak | adya | devavyacaḥ-tamaḥ
